more.question: N5
more.good_when: A maintainer reading the test names finds a test for every case that the docstrings state, so a failure names the case that broke. Today these stated cases have no test of their own: a refund or credit line whose amount reaches -1000000000 is refused while one just above it is taken, with only the positive end tested; a quantity at -1000000000 is refused while -999999999 is taken, again with only the positive end tested; a quantity written in another script's digits, such as Arabic-Indic digits, is refused, as lines.py's comment says it must be; and the spaces around each cell are dropped, which the docstring states but which only shows up unnamed inside test_reads_each_row_as_a_line, as the trailing space of `Design `. The help that `invoicer --help` prints is how an accounting colleague learns the row form `<description>;<price>;<quantity>` and that the rate is a percent such as 19, yet no case names what it shows.

more.question: N7
more.good_when: A maintainer who breaks any behavior sees a test fail. Today some changes pass all 70 tests unnoticed (each checked by changing the code in a throwaway copy, and coverage.py with branch coverage): letting a quantity in other scripts' digits through, so that `Design;100.00;٣` prints a line of 3; checking the amount limit on the positive side only, so that a credit of -1999999999.98 prints; dropping the row form from the LINES help, the percent wording from the --rate help, or the command's description from `invoicer --help`; and changing what a Line looks like when printed for debugging, which is invoicer/lines.py line 37, the one line that no test runs. Once these are covered, each of those breaks fails a test that names its case.
